        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: napi-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-out/*.node
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Build and archive the release artifact
        if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cargo_bin=cargo
          if [[ "$USE_CROSS" == true ]]; then cargo_bin=cross; fi
          cd "${PACKAGE_DIR:-.}"
          "$cargo_bin" build --release --locked --target "$TRIPLE" --package "$PACKAGE"
          metadata=$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1)
          target_dir=$(jq -r .target_directory <<< "$metadata")
          temp=$RUNNER_TEMP
          if command -v cygpath > /dev/null; then target_dir=$(cygpath -u "$target_dir"); temp=$(cygpath -u "$temp"); fi
          case "$TRIPLE" in *windows*) suffix=.exe ;; wasm32-*) suffix=.wasm ;; *) suffix= ;; esac
          stage="$temp/release-stage"
          out="$temp/release-assets"
          mkdir -p "$stage" "$out"
          jq -r --arg package "$PACKAGE" '.packages[] | select(.name == $package) | .targets[]
            | select(.kind | index("bin")) | .name' <<< "$metadata" | while IFS= read -r bin; do
            cp "$target_dir/$TRIPLE/release/$bin$suffix" "$stage/"
          done
          if [[ -z "$(ls -A "$stage")" ]]; then
            echo "::error::$PACKAGE builds no binary target for $TRIPLE"
            exit 1
          fi
          cd "$stage"
          case "$ASSET" in
            *.tar.gz | *.tgz) tar -czf "$out/$ASSET" ./* ;;
            *.tar.xz) tar -cJf "$out/$ASSET" ./* ;;
            *.zip) if command -v zip > /dev/null; then zip -q "$out/$ASSET" ./*; else 7z a -bd "$out/$ASSET" ./* > /dev/null; fi ;;
            *)
              binaries=(./*)
              if [[ ${#binaries[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
                echo "::error::$ASSET is not an archive name, but $PACKAGE builds ${#binaries[@]} binaries"
                exit 1
              fi
              cp "${binaries[0]}" "$out/$ASSET"
              ;;
          esac
      - if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/${{ matrix.artifactName }}
      - if: matrix.kind == 'cargo'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: asset-${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets/${{ matrix.artifactName }}
          if-no-files-found: error

  # No registry credentials: the executing job uploads these exact files.
  build-python:
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: {contents: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0, persist-credentials: false}
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@3feff402ea4798c4708ec6fa09e402b956596598 # callisto@0.14.0
        with: {version: callisto@0.14.0}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Build the Python distributions
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet build==1.4.4
          export PATH="$RUNNER_TEMP/build-venv/bin:$PATH"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/python-dist"
          callisto release build-python --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" \
            --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/python-dist"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: python-dist
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/python-dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error

  execute:
    needs: [plan, build, build-python]
    # A skipped build blocks only when it had nothing to build.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      (needs.build.result == 'success' || (needs.build.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.matrix == '[]')) &&
      (needs.build-python.result == 'success' || (needs.build-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.plan.outputs.has_python != 'true'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency: {group: callisto-release-execute, cancel-in-progress: false}
    permissions: {contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: read}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with: {fetch-depth: 0} # zizmor: ignore[artipacked] tag push needs persisted credentials
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@3feff402ea4798c4708ec6fa09e402b956596598 # callisto@0.14.0
        with: {version: callisto@0.14.0}
      - name: Install twine
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/publish-venv"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/publish-venv/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet twine==7.0.0
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/publish-venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      # Downloads land under $RUNNER_TEMP: `release execute` requires a clean worktree.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: napi-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/napi-artifacts
      - name: Place napi artifacts
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_napi == 'true'
        env:
          NAPI_DIRS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.napi_dirs }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          jq -r '.[]' <<< "$NAPI_DIRS" | while IFS= read -r dir; do
            npx --yes --package @napi-rs/cli@3.10.4 napi artifacts --cwd "${dir:-.}" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/napi-artifacts"
          done
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          pattern: asset-*
          merge-multiple: true
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: python-dist
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-assets
      - name: Write the artifact manifest
        if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' || needs.plan.outputs.has_python == 'true'
        env:
          HAS_PYTHON: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_python }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets"
            --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json")
          if [[ "$HAS_PYTHON" == true ]]; then args+=(--seal-python); fi
          callisto release artifact-manifest "${args[@]}"
      - name: Execute the release
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          args=(--intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json"
            --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-assets")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

content.content:
name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, moon and the .prototools toolchain, and Callisto CLI'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: auto installs the requested release version; local builds validated Callisto checkout source and ignores version. Release jobs must use local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: >-
      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's
      own invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling
      back to the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  verification:
    description: >-
      Attestation verification of the prebuilt release asset (gh attestation verify, repo
      orin-dx/callisto, signer workflow callisto-release.yml). One of: require = a failed
      verification or missing gh aborts the step and the asset is never run; fallback (default) =
      on failure or missing gh, warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io instead (never
      run the unverified asset); skip = do not verify, warn, and use the asset. Releases built
      before the first attested release carry no attestation, hence the fallback default.
    required: false
    default: 'fallback'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION: ${{ inputs.verification }}
        GITHUB_ACTION_REF: ${{ github.action_ref }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/install-callisto.sh" # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.
name: 'Callisto Validate Action'
description: 'Validates pending changesets, package discovery, configuration health, and release plan DAG'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Setup Callisto Environment
      uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto

    - name: Validate Configuration, Package Discovery & Changesets
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      # `callisto status --check` is a conventional
      # 0/1 gate: 0 when there are no error-level diagnostics, 1 otherwise,
      # regardless of pending changesets. `shell: bash` already fails the step
      # on a non-zero exit, so no wrapper is needed.
      run: callisto status --check

    - name: Pre-Flight Release Plan Simulation (DAG Pre-Check)
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        echo "::group::Simulating Release Plan"
        callisto release --dry-run --format text
        echo "::endgroup::"

    - name: Render PR Release Pre-Flight Summary
      shell: bash
      env:
        FORCE_COLOR: "1"
        CLICOLOR_FORCE: "1"
      run: |
        echo "### Callisto Release Pre-Flight Verification" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Package Discovery**: All workspace crates and packages are correctly tracked." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Configuration Health**: \`callisto.toml\` schema and rules are valid." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "- **Changeset Integrity**: Pending changesets are valid." >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo "#### Workspace Package Status" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        callisto status >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
        echo '```' >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY

3:Registry credential setup only. For the release lifecycle itself (local `callisto release`, generated workflows, recovery, execution semantics), see [`releasing.md`](releasing.md). For the `[registries.<name>]` config schema, see [`config.md`](config.md).
9:## First publish
11:A package that has never been published is released from its manifest version with no changeset. Callisto plans it like any other release, and the first publish is the one most likely to fail for reasons outside Callisto:
15:- **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.
56:- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
71:- run: callisto release execute --intent "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-intent/release-intent.json" --receipt "$RUNNER_TEMP/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$GITHUB_SHA"
89:Give the `execute` job `permissions: id-token: write` and set `NPM_CONFIG_PROVENANCE: "true"` in its env. npm then attests each package to the workflow run and commit; Callisto needs no flag.
95:Set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` as a repository secret and pass it to the job environment:
99:  CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
122:Generated release workflows accept `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, and `PYPI_TOKEN` as secrets. They supply each token only during publishing. Custom npm registries need their own native configuration.
132:- A sealed build is used only by the generated build-matrix workflow, which builds in a `build-python` job without credentials and seals the files in the manifest. The generated execute job installs a pinned `twine` into a venv on its PATH; a hand-written workflow must provide `twine` itself. Sealing is opt-in at execution: a manifest that seals no Python files, or no manifest at all, builds in the executing job and warns. A sealed file the index serves without a sha256 is treated as differing. A workspace whose only release work is Python uses the single-job workflow, which installs pinned `build` and `twine` before the release step, and is not sealed. With a sealed build the run uploads exactly the built files, and a file on the index under a sealed name with different bytes stops the release (E307).

11:`callisto release` selects packages without a tag for their current version. It publishes to registries, creates tags and GitHub releases, and records HEAD as the source. It can run on any branch.
13:- `callisto release --dry-run` prints the plan and performs no effect. It works anywhere, including on a dirty worktree or without an `origin` remote (tags are then noted as unbound).
16:- It prints `Nothing to release.` and exits 0 when every package is already tagged.
17:- It prints a summary. With `--receipt <file>` it also writes the receipt there, only when every selected operation succeeded. An existing tag can exclude unfinished work before those operations are selected; see the retry limit below.
22:A local release refuses with E320, before any effect, when the registry already holds a version it would release but the package's files changed since the commit that set that version, or no commit in this history sets it. Check out the version commit the error names and run `callisto release` again: it adopts the published version and tags that commit. When no commit is named, check out the commit that was published, or tag it by hand.
26:If a local release tags a version but fails before pushing the tag or completing GitHub work, a fresh `callisto release` at the same commit lists the package again, observes each remaining effect and finishes it.
28:- `Nothing to release.` is not proof of completion for a tag on an older commit: the retry looks only at tags on the commit being released.
40:- **Simple shape** (no artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr` maintains the release PR. On each default-branch push, `release` runs `callisto release`; it is a no-op until an untagged version is merged.
48:- Cargo `bin` targets can become GitHub release assets. npm `bin` and Python `[project.scripts]` are registry releases, not artifact products (E304).
55:Pin the Callisto actions by commit with the version in a comment, such as `uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@1.0.0`. The action installs the release that commit belongs to. From 1.0.0 the floating tag `v1` also works (`@v1`): each stable 1.x release moves it to its release commit, never backwards, and the action installs that release. A mutable tag is only as safe as the repository that moves it, so a pinned commit stays the stricter choice.
75:After a failed committed-decision CI release, "Re-run failed jobs" adopts completed effects and performs the rest. A green workflow alone is not proof of publication: check the receipt and providers.
82:- `callisto release --dry-run --format text` — simulates the release plan without effect.
87:## Release identity and recovery
94:A recovery is a new run using current orchestration and the merged release PR's full source SHA. It does not rerun historical workflow code or invent a newer version. Callisto's own workflow asks [`callisto release pending`](#finding-releases-that-did-not-finish) for the oldest unfinished release on each main push. It verifies that SHA against the merged managed PR and the current main history before planning. After a release executes, the workflow dispatches the next unfinished one, or refreshes the release PR for newer changesets when none remains.
96:To retry a failed run for the same source, use "Re-run failed jobs" or dispatch the workflow on main with `release_source_sha=<merged PR merge SHA>`. Matching completed effects are adopted; conflicting or uncertain results stop the run. A receipt is written only after every selected operation succeeds. The merge SHA is available in the PR's merge commit and does not depend on a proposed version tag. Release runs execute one at a time: a push during a release waits, then finds nothing pending. A dispatch with an explicit SHA queued behind a push can be replaced by it, so dispatch it again if it did not start.
98:A failed release is selected again on every main push until it finishes, which also holds back the release PR refresh. To get past one you finished by hand, push its missing tags, or run `callisto release pending --from <newer release sha>`. Otherwise recover it with a dispatch of its SHA (see [recovering an older release](#recovering-an-older-release)). Finish an older unpublished release before merging a newer release PR: the newer one publishes without any warning that the older version was never tagged.
104:`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.
107:callisto release pending                    # text
108:callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
109:callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
112:Recover each one with the dispatch below, oldest first.
114:## Recovering an older release
116:Recovering a commit that is no longer a branch tip may require these manual actions:
118:**E180: the workflow can't push tags.** GitHub rejects a `GITHUB_TOKEN` tag push when the tagged commit's workflows differ from every branch tip. Push every tag of the release yourself (PAT or deploy key), then dispatch the release for that SHA:
122:git tag -a "<tag>" -m "Release <tag>" "$SHA"   # each tag of the release
123:git push origin "<tag>"
130:gh release delete-asset "<release tag>" "<asset>" --yes   # each mismatched asset
136:Callisto checks the registry, remote tag, and GitHub release before each effect. An exact match is adopted; a conflict or uncertain result stops the run. Check the receipt and providers before treating a release as complete.
138:Registry checks confirm version presence, not identical bytes or the npm dist-tag. A Python release is complete only when every built wheel and sdist is on the index; a partly uploaded one is finished by uploading the missing files, and a sealed build also compares each file's digest. See [publishing limits](publishing.md#current-python-support-limits).
140:GitHub Releases start as drafts. Assets upload before the release is made public.
153:For a package with both Cargo and npm distributions, one registry publish can still lag behind its shared tag or public GitHub release. Do not treat that announcement as proof that both distributions are available.

+## First publish
+
+A package that has never been published is released from its manifest version with no changeset. Callisto plans it like any other release, and the first publish is the one most likely to fail for reasons outside Callisto:

+- **Fill in the metadata the registry requires.** crates.io needs `description` and `license` (or `license-file`) in `Cargo.toml`. A first release of a crate without them stops with E323 before anything is published.
+- **Use a token that can create the package.** A token scoped to existing packages cannot publish a new one. Trusted publishing (OIDC) is configured per package on the registry and generally needs the package, or a pending publisher, to exist first, so plan on one token-based first publish. Follow each registry's current documentation.
+- **Package managers.** An npm package is published with the manager its workspace uses (`npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn` 4 or `bun`), passing `--tag`, `--access` and, where the manager takes one, `--registry`. Yarn takes no `--registry`; it reads `publishConfig.registry` from the package itself.

+- **Rehearse.** `callisto release --dry-run` shows what would be published and in which order, and works without credentials.
+
+## Pulling a release
+
+Callisto never deletes, yanks or deprecates anything. Pulling a release is a manual registry action, and the version stays used:
+
+| Registry | Soft pull | Delete |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| crates.io | `cargo yank` hides it from new resolution; it stays downloadable and existing lockfiles keep working. | Limited to 72 hours after publishing, or a single owner, few downloads and no dependents. |
+| npm | `npm deprecate` keeps it installable with a warning. | `npm unpublish` within 72 hours if nothing depends on it; later only with no dependents, under 300 weekly downloads and a single owner. +| PyPI | Yank (PEP 592) hides it from normal resolution. | Permanent. A filename cannot be reused even after deletion, and deleting a project frees its name for anyone. |

Otherwise recover it with a dispatch of its SHA (see [recovering an older release](#recovering-an-older-release)). Finish an older unpublished release before merging a newer release PR: the newer one publishes without any warning that the older version was never tagged.
 
 Callisto waits for a published version to appear before it announces anything: up to 6 minutes for npm and PyPI, 2 for Cargo. npm packages are published back to back and waited for together, so a release of many npm packages waits once, not once per package; Cargo and PyPI publishes are waited for as they are published. If the registry is slower it stops with E157; re-run the failed job once the version shows, or set `confirm-timeout` on the registry in `callisto.toml` (see [configuration](config.md#registries)) and keep the job's `timeout-minutes` above the total wait.
 
+## Finding releases that did not finish
+
+`callisto release pending` lists the merged release commits whose release did not finish, oldest first, with what is missing. It reads each release commit's committed decision and checks that every package has its tag and every GitHub release is published, so it needs no checkout of the old commit and publishes nothing. A release publishes to the registries before it tags, so a missing tag means the release stopped early.

+callisto --format json release pending      # for a workflow
+callisto release pending --from <sha>       # skip an older release that cannot finish
